definition: In machine learning and natural language processing, the pachinko allocation model (PAM) is a topic model.
details: Topic models are a suite of algorithms to uncover the hidden thematic structure of a collection of documents. The algorithm improves upon earlier topic models such as latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) by modeling correlations between topics in addition to the word correlations which constitute topics. PAM provides more flexibility and greater expressive power than latent Dirichlet allocation. While first described and implemented in the context of natural language processing, the algorithm may have applications in other fields such as bioinformatics. The model is named for pachinko machines—a game popular in Japan, in which metal balls bounce down around a complex collection of pins until they land in various bins at the bottom.

explainer.lead: Pachinko allocation is a topic model that uncovers the hidden thematic structure of a document collection. It improves on earlier models such as LDA by modeling correlations between topics as well as word correlations.

tiers.eli5: It is like sorting a library into subjects while also noting which subjects tend to appear together.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers apply it where topic relationships matter, gaining more flexibility and expressive power than LDA. A pitfall is the added model complexity, which can be harder to fit and interpret than simpler topic models.
tiers.paperLevel: PAM is a topic model that improves on latent Dirichlet allocation by modeling correlations between topics in addition to word correlations, giving greater flexibility and expressive power; it was first described in natural language processing and may extend elsewhere.

explainer.example: On a news archive, PAM groups articles into topics and captures that 'elections' and 'economy' co-occur more than 'elections' and 'sports'.
